source_text: Si Paulo lex spiritalis, et benedictiones spiritales. Non solum terrae fructus sed animae victoria.
thought_title: If the law is spiritual for Paul, blessings are spiritual too
orientation: Origen is opening a new homily by arguing from Paul's authority that the law's blessings must be understood spiritually, not as earthly rewards.
pass_a_gloss: If [to] Paul [the] law [is] spiritual, and [the] blessings [are] spiritual. Not only [of the] earth [the] fruits but [of the] soul [the] victory.

choices.english: If the law is spiritual for Paul
choices.why: The dative Paulo marks the authority to whom the law is spiritual; the conditional si opens the inference.
rejected: If Paul says the law is spiritual
If the law is spiritual according to Paul

choices.why: The et is connective and the predicate adjective spiritales is supplied from the previous clause; the sense is that the blessings of the law share the same spiritual character.

choices.term: Non solum terrae fructus sed animae victoria
choices.english: Not only the fruits of the earth but the victory of the soul
choices.why: The contrast non solum...sed marks the replacement of a literal earthly reading with a spiritual one; victoria animae is the spiritual counterpart to terrae fructus.
rejected: Not only the fruits of the land but the soul's victory
Not only earthly fruits but the victory of the spirit

pass_b_english: If the law is spiritual for Paul, then its blessings are spiritual as well—not only the fruits of the earth, but the victory of the soul.

last_rejected.quote: If the law is spiritual for Paul
last_rejected.why: Source says law is spiritual 'to/for Paul', not that Paul holds this opinion; English makes Paul the subject of belief.
last_rejected.fix: If for Paul the law is spiritual, then its blessings are spiritual too.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Si Paulo lex spiritalis' naturally means 'if the law is spiritual for Paul'; English correctly renders the dative, no meaning changed.
